title: Boolean logic: AND, OR, NOT
subtitle: The binary building blocks of digital thought

learn.prompt: An AND gate requires all of its inputs to be high (1) to produce a high output. Configure inputs A and B so the AND gate turns ON.
learn.hint: An AND gate outputs 1 only when Input A = 1 AND Input B = 1.
learn.explanation: True AND True = True. If either input is False, the AND gate outputs False.

learn.prompt: Input A is FALSE (0) and Input B is TRUE (1). What is the output of an OR gate?
learn.hint: An OR gate outputs TRUE if AT LEAST ONE input is TRUE.
learn.explanation: 0 OR 1 = 1. An OR gate only outputs FALSE when both inputs are FALSE.

misconceptionMap.false: An OR gate is satisfied whenever any input is 1.
misconceptionMap.unknown: Digital logic is deterministic and fully resolved.
misconceptionMap.high-z: The output of an active gate drives a solid voltage level.

learn.prompt: A NOT gate (inverter) receives an input of TRUE (1). What does it output?
learn.hint: A NOT gate inverts its input: 1 becomes 0, and 0 becomes 1.

misconceptionMap.true: A NOT gate inverts the signal; it never passes it unchanged.
misconceptionMap.two: Binary logic values are strictly 0 and 1.

learn.prompt: In binary Boolean notation, evaluate: 1 * (0 + 1). (Where * denotes AND, + denotes OR).

check.prompt: Which logic gate outputs TRUE only when BOTH of its inputs are TRUE?
check.hint: Think of two switches in series.
check.explanation: An AND gate is the conjunction operator: A AND B is true only when both operands are true.

misconceptionMap.or: An OR gate also outputs TRUE if only one input is TRUE.
misconceptionMap.not: A NOT gate has only one input.
misconceptionMap.buffer: A buffer simply copies a single input.

check.prompt: If A = 1 and B = 0, what is NOT(A AND B)?
check.hint: First evaluate A AND B, then invert the result.
check.explanation: A AND B = 1 AND 0 = 0. Inverting with NOT gives NOT(0) = 1 (TRUE). This is a NAND operation.

misconceptionMap.false: Remember to invert the result of the AND with the outer NOT.
misconceptionMap.minus-one: Boolean inversion produces 1, not arithmetic negation.

takeaway.title: The triumvirate of Boolean logic
takeaway.body: Every computer on Earth is built from three elementary logical operations: AND (both must hold), OR (at least one must hold), and NOT (inversion). Combined, they can express any computable algorithm.
